title.zh: 卷二 梁書2: 太祖本紀二
title.en: Volume 2 Book of Later Liang 2: Taizu Annals 2
title.raw: 卷二 梁書2: 太祖本紀二 Volume 2 Book of Later Liang 2: Taizu Annals 2

sentences.zh: 二年正月，淮南楊行密舉全吳之眾，精甲五萬，以伐徐州，帝領大軍禦之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Yang Xingmi of Huainan raised all the forces of Wu—fifty thousand picked armored men—to attack Xuzhou; the Emperor led a great army to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Yang Xingmi of Huainan mustered all Wu with fifty thousand elite armored troops and marched on Xuzhou; the Emperor took the field in force to meet him.

sentences.zh: 行密聞帝親征，乃收軍而退。

translations.literal: When Xingmi heard the Emperor was campaigning in person, he withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the Emperor had come in person, Xingmi pulled his army back.

sentences.zh: 時幽州節度使劉仁恭大舉蕃漢兵號十萬以伐魏，遂攻陷貝州，州民萬餘戶，無少長悉屠之。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Rengong, military governor of Youzhou, raised a great force of tribal and Han troops numbering one hundred thousand to attack Wei, captured Beizhou, and of more than ten thousand households in the prefecture, none young or old was spared slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong of Youzhou then raised a mixed tribal and Han host said to number one hundred thousand against Wei, took Beizhou, and slaughtered every soul among its ten thousand-odd households.

sentences.zh: 進攻魏州，魏人來乞師，帝遣硃友倫、張存敬、李思安等先屯于內黃，帝遂親征。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Weizhou, the people of Wei came to beg for aid; the Emperor sent Zhu Youlun, Zhang Cunjing, Li Si'an, and others to encamp first at Neihuang, then the Emperor himself campaigned.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei sought help against the siege, the Emperor sent Zhu Youlun, Zhang Cunjing, and Li Si'an ahead to Neihuang and followed in person.

sentences.zh: 三月，與燕軍戰于內黃北，燕軍大敗，殺二萬餘眾，奪馬二千餘匹，擒都將單無敵已下七十餘人。

translations.literal: In the third month he fought the Yan army north of Neihuang; the Yan army was greatly defeated—more than twenty thousand killed, over two thousand horses captured, and more than seventy commanders from Commander Dan Wudi down were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he routed the Yan army north of Neihuang, killing twenty thousand, seizing two thousand horses, and capturing seventy-odd officers down to the famed commander Dan Wudi.

sentences.zh: 《通鑒》：單可及，幽州驍將，號單無敵。

translations.literal: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: Dan Keji was a fierce general of Youzhou, styled Dan Wudi ("Peerless Dan").
translations.idiomatic: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 notes that Dan Keji was a Youzhou champion known as Dan Wudi—"Peerless Dan."

sentences.zh: 是月，葛從周自山東領其部眾，馳以救魏。

translations.literal: That month Ge Congzhou led his troops from Shandong at forced march to relieve Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Ge Congzhou raced from Shandong with his division to relieve Wei.

sentences.zh: 翼日，乘勝，諸將張存敬以下連破八寨，遂逐燕軍，北至於臨清，壅其殘寇於御河，溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The next day, pressing the victory, the generals from Zhang Cunjing downward broke eight camps in succession, pursued the Yan army north to Linqing, blocked the remnant bandits in the Imperial Canal, and very many drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, riding the victory, Zhang Cunjing and the other generals stormed eight camps in a row, drove the Yan army to Linqing, and drowned masses of fugitives in the Imperial Canal.

sentences.zh: 仁恭奔於滄州。

translations.literal: Rengong fled to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong fled to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝表丁會為潞州節度使，以李罕之疾亟故也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor memorialized to appoint Ding Hui military governor of Luzhou, because Li Hanzhi's illness was acute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Emperor recommended Ding Hui as governor of Luzhou, Li Hanzhi being gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 又遣葛從周由固鎮路入於潞州，以援丁會。

translations.literal: He also sent Ge Congzhou by the Guzhen route into Luzhou to reinforce Ding Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Ge Congzhou through Guzhen into Luzhou to reinforce Ding Hui.

sentences.zh: 七月壬辰朔，海州陳漢賓擁所部三千奔於淮南。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month (rengchen), Chen Hanbin of Haizhou led his three thousand troops in flight to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On rengchen, the first of the seventh month, Haizhou's Chen Hanbin defected south with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，晉人陷澤州。

translations.literal: On wuxu the Jin forces captured Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the Jin took Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 帝遣召葛從周於潞，留賀德倫以守之。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Ge Congzhou back from Luzhou and left He Delun to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor recalled Ge Congzhou from Luzhou and left He Delun to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 未幾，德倫為晉人所逼，遂棄潞而歸，由是潞州復為晉人所有。

translations.literal: Before long Delun was pressed by the Jin forces, abandoned Luzhou and returned, and thus Luzhou again fell to the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon pressed by the Jin, Delun abandoned Luzhou; the prefecture was Jin's again.

sentences.zh: 十一月，陝州都將硃簡殺留後李璠，自稱留後，送款於帝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zhu Jian, garrison commander of Shanzhou, killed the acting governor Li Fan, declared himself acting governor, and submitted allegiance to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Shanzhou commander Zhu Jian killed acting governor Li Fan, seized the post, and submitted to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，遣葛從周以兗、鄆、滑、魏之師伐滄州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou with armies from Yan, Yun, Hua, and Wei to attack Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou with troops from Yan, Yun, Hua, and Wei against Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月庚寅，攻德州，拔之，梟刺史傅公和於城上。

translations.literal: On gengyin in the fifth month he attacked Dezhou, captured it, and displayed the head of Prefect Fu Gonghe on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin in the fifth month he stormed Dezhou, took it, and exposed Prefect Fu Gonghe's head on the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 己亥，進攻浮陽。

translations.literal: On jihai he advanced to attack Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he pressed the attack on Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 六月，燕帥劉仁恭大舉來援，從周與諸將逆戰于乾寧軍老鴉堤，大破之，殺萬餘眾，俘其將佐馬慎交已下百餘人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Yan commander Liu Rengong came in force to relieve them; Congzhou and the generals met them in battle at Laoya Embankment in Qianning Army, routed them greatly, killed more than ten thousand, and captured over a hundred of their officers including Ma Shenjiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Liu Rengong marched to relieve the city; Congzhou met him at Laoya Embankment in Qianning Army, crushed his host, killed ten thousand, and took a hundred-odd officers including Ma Shenjiao.

sentences.zh: 既而以連雨，遂班師。

translations.literal: Thereafter because of continuous rain, the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Relentless rain then forced a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 八月，河東遣李進通襲陷洺州，執刺史硃紹宗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Hedong sent Li Jintong in a surprise attack that captured Mingzhou and seized Prefect Zhu Shaozong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Hedong's Li Jintong raided and took Mingzhou, capturing Prefect Zhu Shaozong.

sentences.zh: 帝遣葛從周自鄴縣渡漳水，屯於黃龍鎮，親領中軍涉洺而寨；

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Ge Congzhou from Yexian to cross the Zhang River and encamp at Huanglong Fort; he personally led the central army across the Ming River to make camp;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Ge Congzhou from Yexian across the Zhang to Huanglong Fort while he led the center across the Ming to encamp;

sentences.zh: 晉人懼而宵遁，洺州復平。

translations.literal: the Jin forces fled by night in fear, and Mingzhou was pacified again.
translations.idiomatic: the Jin fled overnight in panic and Mingzhou was restored.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝以仁恭、進通之入寇也，皆由鎮、定為其囊橐，即以葛從周為上將以伐鎮州，遂攻下臨城，渡滹沱以環其城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because Rengong's and Jintong's invasions had both drawn on Zhen and Ding as their storehouses, he made Ge Congzhou supreme commander to attack Zhenzhou, captured Lincheng, and crossed the Hutuo to surround the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, blaming Zhen and Ding for supplying Rengong and Jintong, he made Ge Congzhou supreme commander against Zhenzhou, took Lincheng, and crossed the Hutuo to invest the city.

sentences.zh: 帝親領軍繼至，鎮帥王熔俱，納質請盟，仍獻文繒二十萬以犒戎士，帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally led the army to follow; the Zhen commander Wang Rong submitted hostages and begged alliance, and also presented two hundred thousand bolts of figured silk to reward the troops; the Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed in person; Wang Rong of Zhen sent hostages, sued for peace, and offered two hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army—the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十月，晉人以帝宿兵于趙，遂南下太行，急攻河陽，留後侯言與都將閻寶力戰固守，僅而獲全。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Jin, because the Emperor was encamped in Zhao, marched south through the Taihang in haste and attacked Heyang urgently; the acting governor Hou Yan and Commander Yan Bao fought stubbornly to hold firm and barely survived intact.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, with the Emperor camped in Zhao, the Jin rushed south through the Taihang and hammered Heyang; Hou Yan and Yan Bao held on by sheer force and barely kept the city.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以張存敬為上將，自甘陵發軍，北侵幽、薊，連拔瀛、莫二郡，遂移軍以攻中山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he made Zhang Cunjing supreme commander, launched the army from Ganling, invaded You and Ji to the north, captured Ying and Mo in succession, and then shifted the army to attack Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhang Cunjing marched from Ganling north into You and Ji, took Ying and Mo in turn, then turned on Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 定帥王郜以精甲二萬戰於懷德亭，盡殪之。

translations.literal: The Ding commander Wang Gao fought with twenty thousand picked armored troops at Huaide Pavilion; they were utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Ding's Wang Gao met him at Huaide Pavilion with twenty thousand elite armored troops and was annihilated.

sentences.zh: 郜懼，奔於太原。

translations.literal: Gao in fear fled to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao fled in terror to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 遲明，大軍集於城下，郜季父處直持印鑰乞降，亦以繒帛三十萬為獻，帝即以處直代郜領其鎮焉。

translations.literal: At daybreak the great army gathered below the city; Gao's uncle by descent Chuzhi held out the seal and keys to beg surrender, and also presented three hundred thousand bolts of silk as tribute; the Emperor at once had Chuzhi replace Gao in command of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn the army stood before the walls; Gao's uncle Wang Chuzhi came out with seal and keys to surrender and gave three hundred thousand bolts of silk—the Emperor installed Chuzhi in Gao's place.

sentences.zh: 是月，燕人劉守光赴援中山，寨于易水之上，繼為康懷英、張存敬等所敗，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: That month the Yan man Liu Shouguang came to relieve Zhongshan and encamped above the Yishui; he was thereafter defeated by Kang Huaiying, Zhang Cunjing, and others, and very many were killed or captured.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liu Shouguang of Yan marched to save Zhongshan and camped on the Yishui; Kang Huaiying and Zhang Cunjing broke him with heavy slaughter.

sentences.zh: 由是河朔知懼，皆弭伏焉。

translations.literal: From this the Hebei region knew fear and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all Hebei submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 是歲，唐左軍中尉劉季述幽昭宗於東宮內，立皇子德王裕為帝，仍遣其養子希度來言，願以唐之神器輸於帝。

translations.literal: That year the Tang Left Army Commissioner Liu Jishu confined Zhaozong in the Eastern Palace, installed the princely son Prince De Wang Yu as emperor, and still sent his adopted son Xidu to declare that he wished to hand over the Tang regalia to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Jishu, Tang's Left Army Commissioner, imprisoned Zhaozong in the Eastern Palace, set up Prince De Wang Yu as emperor, and sent his adopted son Xidu to offer the Tang regalia to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝時方在河朔，聞之，遽還於汴，大計未決。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then in Hebei; when he heard it he hastened back to Bian, but no great decision had been reached.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was in Hebei; hearing the news he hurried back to Bian, still undecided on a course.

sentences.zh: 會李振自長安使回，因言於帝曰：「夫豎刁、伊戾之亂，所以資霸者之事也。

translations.literal: When Li Zhen returned from an embassy to Chang'an, he therefore said to the Emperor: "The disorders of Duke Huan of Qi's favorites and of Yi Li are precisely what supply a hegemon's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen returned from Chang'an and told the Emperor: "The chaos of Duke Huan's favorites and of Yi Li is exactly what makes a hegemon's opportunity.

sentences.zh: 今閹豎幽辱天子，王不能討，無以令諸侯。

translations.literal: Now the eunuchs have imprisoned and shamed the Son of Heaven; if Your Highness cannot punish them, you cannot command the feudatories."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs now hold the Son of Heaven in shame; unless you punish them, you cannot command the lords."

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，因請振復使于長安，與時宰潛謀反正。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood, and therefore asked Zhen to go again as envoy to Chang'an and secretly plot restoration with the chief ministers of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took the point and sent Zhen back to Chang'an to plot restoration with the chief ministers in secret.

sentences.zh: 天復元年正月乙酉朔，唐宰相崔允潛使人以帝密旨告于侍衛軍將孫德昭已下，令誅左右中尉劉季述、王仲先等，即時迎昭宗於東內，禦樓反正。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the first year of Tianfu (yiyou), Tang Chancellor Cui Yun secretly sent men with the Emperor's secret instructions to the Palace Guard generals from Sun Dezhao down, ordering them to execute the Left and Right Army Commissioners Liu Jishu, Wang Zhongxian, and others, and at once welcome Zhaozong from the Eastern Palace and ascend the tower to restore right rule.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, New Year's Day of Tianfu 1, Chancellor Cui Yun sent the Emperor's secret orders to Sun Dezhao and the Palace Guard to kill Liu Jishu, Wang Zhongxian, and the other commissioners and restore Zhaozong from the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，降制進封帝為梁王，酬反正之功也。

translations.literal: On guisi an edict was issued promoting the Emperor to Prince of Liang, rewarding the merit of the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi an edict raised the Emperor to Prince of Liang in reward for the restoration.

sentences.zh: 昭宗之廢也，汴之邸吏程岩牽昭宗衣下殿。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong was deposed, Cheng Yan, a clerk at the Bian lodging, pulled Zhaozong's robe to lead him down from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong was deposed, Cheng Yan, a clerk at the Bian lodge, tugged the emperor's robe to hurry him from the hall.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，召岩至汴，折其足，送于長安，杖殺之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it he summoned Yan to Bian, broke his legs, sent him to Chang'an, and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Yan brought to Bian, broke his legs, sent him to Chang'an, and had him clubbed to death.

sentences.zh: 是時，河中節度使王珂結援於太原，帝怒，遣大將張存敬率將涉河，由含山路鼓行而進。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Ke, military governor of Hezhong, had allied with Taiyuan; the Emperor in anger sent the great general Zhang Cunjing leading generals across the river, marching rapidly by the Hanshan route.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke of Hezhong had allied with Taiyuan; enraged, the Emperor sent Zhang Cunjing across the river by the Hanshan road at forced march.

sentences.zh: 戊申，攻下絳州。

translations.literal: On wushen he captured Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen he took Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬子，晉州刺史張漢瑜舉郡來降，帝即以大將侯言權領晉州，何絪權領絳州，晉、絳平。

translations.literal: On renzi Jinzhou Prefect Zhang Hanyu surrendered the whole prefecture; the Emperor at once had the great general Hou Yan act as Jinzhou commander and He Yin act as Jiangzhou commander; Jin and Jiang were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Zhang Hanyu of Jinzhou surrendered his prefecture; the Emperor put Hou Yan in charge of Jinzhou and He Yin of Jiangzhou—both circuits were pacified.

sentences.zh: 己未，大軍至河中，存敬命繚其垣而攻之。

translations.literal: On jiwei the great army reached Hezhong; Cunjing ordered its ramparts invested and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei the main force reached Hezhong; Cunjing ringed the walls and assaulted.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，蒲人颺素幡以請降。

translations.literal: On renxu the men of Pu raised white banners to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the people of Pu raised white flags to surrender.

sentences.zh: 庚午，帝至河中，以張存敬權領河中軍府事，河中平，帝乃東還。

translations.literal: On gengwu the Emperor reached Hezhong, put Zhang Cunjing in charge of the Hezhong military government, Hezhong was pacified, and the Emperor then returned east.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the Emperor entered Hezhong, left Zhang Cunjing to govern the circuit, and turned east.

sentences.zh: 是月，李克用遣牙將張特來聘，請尋舊好，帝亦遣使報命。

translations.literal: That month Li Keyong sent military commissioner Zhang Te on a friendly visit to seek renewed good relations; the Emperor also sent an envoy in reply.
translations.idiomatic: That month Li Keyong sent Zhang Te to reopen relations; the Emperor sent an envoy in reply.

sentences.zh: 三月癸未朔，帝歸自河中。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month (guiwei) the Emperor returned from Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, the first of the third month, the Emperor came back from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 是月，遣大將賀德倫、氏叔琮領大軍以伐太原，叔琮等自太行路入，魏博都將張文恭自磁州新口入，葛從周以兗、鄆之眾自土門路入，洺州刺史張歸厚以本軍自馬嶺入，定州刺史王處直以本軍自飛狐入，晉州侯言自陰地入。

translations.literal: That month he sent the great generals He Delun and Shi Shuzong leading a great army to attack Taiyuan; Shuzong and others entered by the Taihang route, Weibo commander Zhang Wengong entered by Xinkou in Cizhou, Ge Congzhou led the Yan and Yun forces in by the Tumen route, Mingzhou Prefect Zhang Guihou led his own army in by Maling, Dingzhou Prefect Wang Chuzhi led his own army in by Feihu, and Jinzhou's Hou Yan entered by Yindi.
translations.idiomatic: That month he sent He Delun and Shi Shuzong against Taiyuan on six roads: Shuzong through the Taihang, Zhang Wengong through Cizhou's Xinkou, Ge Congzhou through Tumen, Zhang Guihou through Maling, Wang Chuzhi through Feihu, and Hou Yan through Yindi.

sentences.zh: 澤州刺史李存璋棄郡奔歸太原。

translations.literal: Zezhou Prefect Li Cunzhang abandoned the prefecture and fled back to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zezhou's Li Cunzhang abandoned his post and fled to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 叔琮引軍逼潞州，節度使孟遷乞降。

translations.literal: Shuzong led the army to press Luzhou; Military Governor Meng Qian begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzong pressed Luzhou until Governor Meng Qian sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 河東屯將李審建、王周領步軍一萬、騎二千詣叔琮歸命，乃進軍趨太原。

translations.literal: Hedong garrison generals Li Shenjian and Wang Zhou led ten thousand infantry and two thousand cavalry to submit to Shuzong; the army then advanced toward Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjian and Wang Zhou of Hedong brought ten thousand foot and two thousand horse to Shuzong; the host then marched on Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 四月乙卯，大軍出石會關，營於洞渦驛。

translations.literal: On yimao in the fourth month the great army passed Shihui Pass and encamped at Donghuo Post.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the fourth month the army cleared Shihui Pass and camped at Donghuo Post.

sentences.zh: 都將白奉國自井陘入，收承天軍。

translations.literal: Commander Bai Fengguo entered by Jingxing and recovered Chengtian Army.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Fengguo entered by Jingxing and recovered Chengtian Army.

sentences.zh: 張歸厚引兵至遼州，刺史張鄂迎降。

translations.literal: Zhang Guihou led troops to Liaozhou; Prefect Zhang E welcomed them in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guihou reached Liaozhou; Prefect Zhang E surrendered.

sentences.zh: 氏叔琮即日與諸軍至晉陽城下，城中雖時出精騎來戰，然危蹙已甚，將謀遁矣。

translations.literal: Shi Shuzong that same day with the armies reached below Jinyang city; though the city from time to time sent out picked cavalry to fight, yet its peril was already extreme and they were about to plan flight.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shuzong reached Jinyang that day; though the city still sallied with elite cavalry, it was desperate and ready to flee.

sentences.zh: 會叔琮以芻糧不給，遂班師。

translations.literal: But Shuzong, because fodder and grain were insufficient, thereupon withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Short of fodder, Shuzong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五月癸卯，昭宗以帝兼領護國軍節度使、河中尹。

translations.literal: On guimao in the fifth month Zhaozong had the Emperor additionally hold the post of military governor of Huguo Army and prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the fifth month Zhaozong made the Emperor concurrent governor of Huguo and prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 六月庚申，帝發自大樑。

translations.literal: On gengshen in the sixth month the Emperor set out from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the sixth month the Emperor left Daliang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，視事於河中，以素服出郊，拜故節度使王重榮墓。

translations.literal: On dingmao he took up office in Hezhong, went outside the suburbs in plain dress, and paid respects at the tomb of the former military governor Wang Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he assumed office at Hezhong, went out in mourning dress, and bowed at Wang Chongrong's tomb.

sentences.zh: 尋辟其子瓚為節度判官，請故相張浚為重榮撰碑。

translations.literal: Shortly he appointed Chongrong's son Zan as military governor's adjutant and requested the former chancellor Zhang Jun to compose a tomb inscription for Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon made Chongrong's son Zan adjutant and asked the former chancellor Zhang Jun to write his tomb inscription.

sentences.zh: 帝自中和初歸唐，首依重榮，至是思其舊德，故恩禮若是。

translations.literal: Since the Emperor from the beginning of the Zhonghe era had returned to Tang and first relied on Chongrong, at this time he recalled his old kindness, and therefore showed such grace and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had first thrown in his lot with Chongrong when he returned to Tang in the Zhonghe era; now he honored that old debt with such ceremony.

sentences.zh: 七月甲寅，帝東還梁邸。

translations.literal: On jiayin in the seventh month the Emperor returned east to the Liang residence.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the seventh month the Emperor went back east to Liang.

sentences.zh: 十月戊戌，奉密詔赴長安。

translations.literal: On wuxu in the tenth month, obeying a secret edict, he went to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu in the tenth month he marched west on a secret summons to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝廷既誅劉季述，以韓全誨、張宏彥為兩軍中尉，袁易簡、周敬容為樞密使。

translations.literal: At that time the court, having executed Liu Jishu, appointed Han Quanhui and Zhang Hongyan as the two army commissioners and Yuan Yijian and Zhou Jingrong as Palace Secretariat commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The court had killed Liu Jishu and made Han Quanhui and Zhang Hongyan army commissioners and Yuan Yijian and Zhou Jingrong commissioners of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時軍國大政，專委宰相崔允，每事裁抑宦官，宦官側目。

translations.literal: At that time major military and state affairs were entrusted entirely to Chancellor Cui Yun, who in every matter curtailed the eunuchs; the eunuchs glared with hostility.
translations.idiomatic: State and army alike were left to Chancellor Cui Yun, who checked the eunuchs at every turn; they watched him with hatred.

sentences.zh: 允一日於便殿，奏欲盡去之，全誨等屬垣聞之，嘗于昭宗前祈哀自訴。

translations.literal: One day Yun in the Informal Hall memorialized wishing to remove them all; Quanhui and the others listened at the wall, and once pleaded piteously before Zhaozong on their own behalf.
translations.idiomatic: One day in the side hall Yun proposed purging them all; Quanhui and his faction eavesdropped and later begged Zhaozong for mercy.

sentences.zh: 自是昭宗敕允，每有密奏，令進囊封。

translations.literal: From this Zhaozong charged Yun that for every secret memorial he should submit it in a sealed pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong then ordered Yun to seal every secret memorial in a pouch.

sentences.zh: 全誨等乃訪京城美婦人十數以進，使求宮中陰事，昭宗不悟，允謀漸泄。

translations.literal: Quanhui and the others then sought out a dozen or so beautiful women of the capital to present, had them inquire into palace secrets; Zhaozong did not realize it, and Yun's plot gradually leaked.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui planted a dozen beauties in the palace to spy; Zhaozong never caught on, and Yun's plans began to leak.

sentences.zh: 中官視允皆裂，以重賂甘言誘籓臣以為城社，時因燕聚，則相向流涕。

translations.literal: The palace eunuchs all glared at Yun with hatred, used heavy bribes and sweet words to entice the frontier lords as their bulwark, and whenever they gathered at banquets would weep facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs hated Yun, bought frontier lords with gold and flattery, and wept together at their feasts.

sentences.zh: 時允掌三司貨泉，全誨等教禁兵伺允出，聚而呼噪，訴以冬衣減損，又于昭宗前訴之；

translations.literal: At that time Yun controlled the three treasuries' coinage; Quanhui and the others incited the Palace Guard to watch for Yun's going out, gather and shout noisily, complaining that winter clothing had been reduced, and also complained before Zhaozong;
translations.idiomatic: Yun then ran the three treasuries; Quanhui stirred the guards to mob Yun in the street over short winter pay and repeated the charge to Zhaozong;

sentences.zh: 昭宗不得已，罷允知政事。

translations.literal: Zhaozong had no choice and dismissed Yun from participation in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong had no choice but to remove Yun from office.

sentences.zh: 允怒，急召帝請以兵入輔，故有是行。

translations.literal: Yun in anger urgently summoned the Emperor to request troops enter to assist, and therefore there was this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Yun called the Emperor to bring troops to the capital—hence this march.

sentences.zh: 戊申，行次河中。

translations.literal: On wushen the march halted at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen he halted at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 同州留後司馬鄴，華之幕吏也，舉郡來降。

translations.literal: Tongzhou acting governor Sima Ye, a staff clerk of Hua, surrendered the whole prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ye, acting governor of Tongzhou and a former clerk of Hua, surrendered his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，駐軍於渭濱，華帥韓建遣使奉箋納款，又以銀三萬兩助軍。

translations.literal: On xinhai the army encamped on the Wei shore; Hua commander Han Jian sent envoys with a memorial submitting allegiance, and also contributed thirty thousand taels of silver to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he camped on the Wei; Han Jian of Hua submitted and sent thirty thousand taels of silver for the army.

sentences.zh: 是日，行次零口。

translations.literal: That day the march halted at Lingkou.
translations.idiomatic: That day he halted at Lingkou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，聞長安亂，昭宗為閹官韓全誨等劫遷，西幸鳳翔，蓋避帝之兵鋒也。

translations.literal: On guichou he heard of disorder in Chang'an: Zhaozong had been seized and moved by the eunuch Han Quanhui and others, and had gone west in mourning progress to Fengxiang—likely to avoid the Emperor's armed edge.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou word came that eunuchs led by Han Quanhui had seized Zhaozong and fled west to Fengxiang—likely to escape the Emperor's army.

sentences.zh: 翼日，遂命旋師，夕次於赤水。

translations.literal: The next day he thereupon ordered the army to turn back; at evening they halted at Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered the army about; that evening they camped at Chishui.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，大軍集于華州城下，韓建惶駭失措，即以城降。

translations.literal: On yimao the great army gathered below Huazhou city; Han Jian in panic and terror lost his composure and at once surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the host stood before Huazhou; Han Jian panicked and surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝表建權知忠武軍事，促令赴任。

translations.literal: On bingchen the Emperor memorialized to have Jian act as administrator of Zhongwu Army affairs and urged him to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the Emperor had Jian appointed acting administrator of Zhongwu and ordered him to his post.

sentences.zh: 同、華二州平。

translations.literal: Tong and Hua, the two prefectures, were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tong and Hua were pacified.

sentences.zh: 是時，唐太子太師盧知猷等二百六十三人列狀請帝速請迎奉。

translations.literal: At that time Tang Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Lu Zhiyou and two hundred sixty-three others submitted a joint petition asking the Emperor to hasten to request to welcome and escort [the emperor back].
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhiyou, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and two hundred sixty-three officials petitioned the Emperor to hurry to welcome the Son of Heaven home.

sentences.zh: 己未，遂帥諸軍發自赤水。

translations.literal: On jiwei he then led the armies in setting out from Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he marched out from Chishui.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，次於咸陽。

translations.literal: On renxu they halted at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu he halted at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 偵者云：「天子昨暮至岐山，旦日宋文通扈蹕入其闉矣。

translations.literal: Scouts reported: "Yesterday evening the Son of Heaven reached Qishan; at dawn Song Wentong escorted the imperial carriage into its gate."
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported: "The Son of Heaven reached Qishan last night; at dawn Song Wentong escorted him through the gate."

sentences.zh: 」是時，岐人遣大將符道昭領兵萬人屯於武功以拒帝，帝遣康懷英敗之，擄甲士六千餘眾。

translations.literal: At that time the Qi people sent the great general Fu Daozhao leading ten thousand troops to encamp at Wugong to resist the Emperor; the Emperor sent Kang Huaiying to defeat them and captured more than six thousand armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Fu Daozhao with ten thousand men to hold Wugong; the Emperor sent Kang Huaiying to rout him and took six thousand armored prisoners.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，次於岐山，文通遣使奉書自陳其失，請帝入覲。

translations.literal: On yichou they halted at Qishan; Wentong sent envoys with a letter confessing his faults and asking the Emperor to enter for audience.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he camped at Qishan; Wentong sent envoys confessing fault and inviting the Emperor in.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，及岐闉，文通渝約，閉壁不獲通，復次於岐山。

translations.literal: On bingchen they reached the Qi gate; Wentong violated the agreement, closed the walls and would not grant passage, and they encamped again at Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he reached Qi's gate; Wentong broke faith, shut the walls, and the army camped again at Qishan.

sentences.zh: 是時，昭宗累遣使齎硃書御劄賜帝，遣帝收軍還本道。

translations.literal: At that time Zhaozong repeatedly sent envoys bearing vermillion-signed imperial letters bestowed on the Emperor, ordering the Emperor to withdraw the army and return to his original circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong kept sending vermillion imperial letters ordering the Emperor to withdraw to his circuit.

sentences.zh: 帝診之曰：「此必文通、全誨之謀也。

translations.literal: The Emperor diagnosed it and said: "This must be the plot of Wentong and Quanhui.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "This is surely Wentong and Quanhui's doing.

sentences.zh: 」皆不奉詔。

translations.literal: " He did not obey any of the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: They ignored every order.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，飛章奉辭，且移軍北伐。

translations.literal: On guiyou he sent urgent memorials with polite declination and moreover shifted the army north in campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he memorialized his excuses and turned the army north.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，至邠州，節度使李繼徽舉城降。

translations.literal: On yihai he reached Binzhou; Military Governor Li Jihui surrendered the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai he reached Binzhou; Li Jihui surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 繼徽因請去文通所賜李姓，復本宗楊氏，又請納其帑以為質，帝皆從之，仍易其名曰崇本。

translations.literal: Jihui thereupon requested to remove the Li surname bestowed by Wentong, restore his original clan Yang, and also requested to offer his treasury goods as hostage; the Emperor consented to all, and moreover changed his name to Chongben.
translations.idiomatic: Jihui asked to drop the Li surname Wentong had given him, resume the Yang clan, and post his treasury as bond—the Emperor agreed and renamed him Chongben.

sentences.zh: 邠州平。

translations.literal: Binzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Binzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 己丑，唐丞相崔允、京兆尹鄭元規至華州，以速迎奉為請，許之。

translations.literal: On jichou Tang Chancellor Cui Yun and Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao Zheng Yuangui reached Huazhou, requesting speedy welcome and escort; he consented.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Chancellor Cui Yun and Jingzhao prefect Zheng Yuangui came to Huazhou to urge a swift welcome; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，帝復次於武功，岐人堅壁不下，乃回軍於河中。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the Emperor again halted at Wugong; the Qi people held the walls firmly and would not come down, and he therefore turned the army back to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year he camped again at Wugong; Qi held firm, so he withdrew to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 二月，聞晉軍大舉南下，聲言來援鳳翔，帝遣硃友甯帥師會晉州刺史氏叔琮以禦之，帝以大軍繼其後。

translations.literal: In the second month, hearing that the Jin army was marching south in force, claiming to come to relieve Fengxiang, the Emperor sent Zhu Youning to lead troops to join Jin Prefecture governor Shi Shuzong to resist them, and followed with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, word came that the Jin host was driving south in strength, ostensibly to rescue Fengxiang; the Emperor sent Zhu Youning with Shi Shuzong of Jinzhou to meet them and marched behind with the main force.

sentences.zh: 三月，友甯、叔琮與晉軍戰于晉州之北，大敗之，生擒克用男廷鸞。

translations.literal: In the third month, Youning and Shuzong fought the Jin army north of Jin Prefecture, inflicted a great defeat, and took alive Ke Yong's son Tingluan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Youning and Shuzong routed the Jin north of Jinzhou and captured Li Keyong's son Tingluan alive.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，謂左右曰：「此岐人之所恃也，今既如此，岐之變不久矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor rejoiced and said to those around him, "This is what the Qi people relied upon; now that it is so, Qi's collapse will not be long."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was elated and told his attendants, "This was the Qi bulwark—now that it is gone, their fall cannot be far off."

sentences.zh: 」四月，岐人遣符道昭領大軍屯於虢縣，康懷英帥驍騎敗之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Qi sent Fu Daozhao to lead a great army and encamp at Hao County; Kang Huaiying led crack cavalry to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Qi sent Fu Daozhao with a large force to Hao County; Kang Huaiying's elite cavalry broke them.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，唐丞相崔允自華來謁帝，屢述艱運危急，事不可緩；

translations.literal: On dingyou, Tang Chancellor Cui Yun came from Hua to pay homage to the Emperor and repeatedly described how critical and urgent the times were—that the matter could brook no delay;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Chancellor Cui Yun came from Hua to see the Emperor and urged again and again that the crisis admitted no delay;

sentences.zh: 又慮群閹擁昭宗幸蜀，且告帝，帝為動容。

translations.literal: He also feared the eunuch faction would take Emperor Zhaozong to Shu, and told the Emperor so, and the Emperor was moved.
translations.idiomatic: he also warned that the eunuchs might escort Zhaozong into Shu—and the Emperor was visibly shaken.

sentences.zh: 允將辭，啟宴於府署，帝舉酒，允情激於哀，因自持樂板，聲曲以侑酒。

translations.literal: When Yun was about to take leave, he opened a banquet at the prefectural office; the Emperor raised his cup, and Yun, stirred by grief, took up a clapper-board himself and sang to accompany the wine.
translations.idiomatic: As Yun prepared to depart he hosted a farewell feast; the Emperor raised his cup, and Yun, overcome, beat a clapper and sang to the wine.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅，座中以良馬珍玩之物賚，既行，命諸將繕戎具。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded him from his seat with fine horses and precious curios; when he had departed, the Emperor ordered the generals to prepare weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the Emperor gave him fine horses and treasures from the table; once Yun had gone, he ordered the generals to ready arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 五月丁巳，帝復西征。

translations.literal: On dingsi in the fifth month the Emperor again campaigned west.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the fifth month the Emperor marched west again.

sentences.zh: 六月丁丑，次於虢縣。

translations.literal: On dingchou in the sixth month he halted at Hao County.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou in the sixth month he camped at Hao County.

sentences.zh: 癸未，與岐軍大戰，自辰至午，殺萬餘眾，擒其將校數百人，乘勝遂逼其壘。

translations.literal: On guimai he fought a great battle with the Qi army from chen to wu, killing more than ten thousand, capturing several hundred of their officers, and pressing the victory to their ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: On guimai he fought the Qi from morning to noon, killing ten thousand, taking hundreds of officers, and driving to their walls.

sentences.zh: 七月丙午，岐軍復出求戰，帝軍不利。

translations.literal: On bingwu in the seventh month the Qi army came out again seeking battle; the Emperor's army fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu in the seventh month the Qi sallied again; the Emperor's force came off badly.

sentences.zh: 是月，遣孔勍帥師取鳳、隴、成三州，皆下之。

translations.literal: That month he sent Kong Xian to lead troops and take the three prefectures of Feng, Long, and Cheng—all fell.
translations.idiomatic: That month he sent Kong Xian to seize Feng, Long, and Cheng—all three fell.

sentences.zh: 是時，岐人相率結寨于諸山，以避帝軍；

translations.literal: At this time the Qi people successively built stockades in the various mountains to avoid the Emperor's army;
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Qi threw up mountain stockades one after another to dodge the imperial host;

sentences.zh: 帝分兵以討，浹旬之內，並平之。

translations.literal: the Emperor divided his forces to attack them, and within ten days or so all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor split columns against them and within ten days had leveled them all.

sentences.zh: 九月甲戌，帝以岐軍諸寨連結稍盛，因親統千騎登高診之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu in the ninth month, because the Qi stockades linked together were growing somewhat strong, the Emperor personally led a thousand horsemen to ascend high ground and reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu in the ninth month, with Qi camps linking up and growing bolder, he rode out personally with a thousand horse to scout from the heights.

sentences.zh: 時秋空澄霽，煙靄四絕，忽有紫雲如傘蓋，凝于龍旌之上，久之方散，觀者鹹訝之。

translations.literal: The autumn sky was clear and bright, with mist and haze gone on every side, when suddenly purple clouds like a canopy gathered on the dragon banner and long did not disperse; all who saw it marveled.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn sky was crystal clear, the mists gone on every hand, when purple cloud like a canopy settled on the dragon banner and lingered; every witness was astonished.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝以岐人堅壁不戰，且慮師老，思欲旋旆以歸河中，因密召上將數人語其事。

translations.literal: At this time, because the Qi held their walls and would not fight, and fearing his army would grow weary, the Emperor wished to turn the standards and return to Hezhong, and secretly summoned several senior generals to discuss the matter.
translations.idiomatic: With Qi refusing battle and his troops tiring, he thought of withdrawing to Hezhong and quietly called several senior commanders to talk it over.

sentences.zh: 時親從指揮使高季昌獨前出抗言曰：「天下雄傑，窺此舉者一歲矣；

translations.literal: Then the personal attendant Commander Gao Jichang alone stepped forward and spoke against it: "The heroes of the realm have watched this campaign for a year;
translations.idiomatic: Only Gao Jichang of the personal guard stepped forward and objected: "For a year the empire's strongmen have watched this campaign;

sentences.zh: 今岐人已困，願少俟之。

translations.literal: Now the Qi are already trapped—please wait a little longer."
translations.idiomatic: the Qi are spent now—grant them a little more time."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其言，因曰：「兵法貴以正理，以奇勝者詐也，乘機集事，必由是乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his words and said, "In warfare what is esteemed is orthodox principle; victory by surprise is deceit—seizing the moment to gather affairs must follow that path, must it not!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and said, "War prizes the straight fight; surprise is trickery—yet to seize the moment one must use it, must one not!"

sentences.zh: 」乃命季昌密募人入岐以紿之，尋有騎士馬景堅願應命，且曰：「是行也，必無生理，願錄其孥。

translations.literal: He then ordered Jichang secretly to recruit men to enter Qi and deceive them; soon a horseman Ma Jingjian volunteered, saying, "This mission surely means I shall not live—I ask that my wife and children be recorded."
translations.idiomatic: He had Jichang secretly recruit infiltrators; a trooper Ma Jingjian volunteered, saying, "I shall not return—please register my family."

sentences.zh: 」帝淒然止其行，景固請，乃許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, grieved, forbade him to go, but Jing insisted and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, stricken, tried to stop him; Jing pressed on and was allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 明日軍出，《北夢瑣言》云：時因硃友倫總騎軍且至，將大出兵迓之。

translations.literal: The next day the army moved out. The 《Beimeng Suoyan》 says: At that time because Zhu Youlun was about to arrive leading the cavalry host, they would deploy a great force to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the army marched out. The 《Beimeng Suoyan》 notes that Zhu Youlun's cavalry was due, so a great column was sent to meet him.

sentences.zh: 諸寨屏匿如無人，景因躍馬西走，直叩岐闉，詐以軍怨東遁為告，且言列寨尚留萬餘人，俟夕將遁矣，宜速掩之。

translations.literal: The stockades hid behind their screens as if empty; Jing leaped his horse west and rode straight to knock on Qi's gates, falsely reporting that the army resented the march east and was fleeing, and that more than ten thousand remained in the camps awaiting evening to flee—Qi should strike quickly to cover them.
translations.idiomatic: The camps lay silent as if deserted; Jing galloped west to the Qi gate, claiming the troops were deserting east and that ten thousand still in camp would flee at dusk—Qi should strike at once.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞信其言，案：李茂貞即宋文通，此紀前後互異，蓋仍當時軍檄之文，未及改從畫一。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen believed him. Note: Li Maozhen was originally Song Wentong; this annal alternates inconsistently before and after—probably still using military dispatches of the time, not yet unified.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen believed him. Note: Li Maozhen was Song Wentong; the annal is inconsistent here, likely preserving contemporary dispatch wording not yet harmonized.

sentences.zh: 遽啟二扉，悉眾來寇。

translations.literal: He hastily opened two gates and led his full strength to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He flung open two gates and led his full strength out to attack.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍以介馬待之，中軍一鼓，百營俱進，又分遣數騎以據其闉。

translations.literal: The various armies waited on barded horses; the center beat the drum once and a hundred camps advanced together, and several horsemen were also sent to seize the gates.
translations.idiomatic: The hosts waited armored; one drum from center and a hundred camps surged forward, while riders seized the gates.

sentences.zh: 岐人進不能駐其趾，退不能入其壘，殺戮蹂踐，不知其數。

translations.literal: The Qi advanced but could not hold their footing, retreated but could not re-enter their ramparts; slain and trampled, their number was beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi could neither stand nor re-enter their walls; slaughter and trampling left the dead beyond count.

sentences.zh: 茂貞由是喪膽，但閉壁而已。

translations.literal: Maozhen thereby lost heart and only shut his walls.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen lost his nerve and would only hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸卯，鄜帥李周彝《新唐書》作「李茂勳」，茂勳即周彝也。

translations.literal: On guimao in the eleventh month, Bin military governor Li Zhouyi—the 《New Tang History》 writes "Li Maoxun"; Maoxun was Zhouyi.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the eleventh month Bin governor Li Zhouyi—the 《New Tang History》 has "Li Maoxun"; Maoxun is Zhouyi.

sentences.zh: 統兵萬餘人屯於岐之北原，與城中舉烽以相應。

translations.literal: led more than ten thousand troops to encamp on the north plain of Qi and lit beacon fires with the city to coordinate.
translations.idiomatic: He brought ten thousand men to camp on the plain north of Qi and coordinated with beacon fires from the city.

sentences.zh: 翼日，帝以周彝既離本部，鄜畤必無守備，因命孔勍乘虛襲下之。

translations.literal: The next day, because Zhouyi had left his base, Bin and Dan must be undefended, and the Emperor ordered Kong Xian to seize the moment and raid and take it.
translations.idiomatic: Next day, with Zhouyi away from his seat, Bin and Dan would be bare; the Emperor sent Kong Xian to strike and take them.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，鄜州平。

translations.literal: On jiayin Bin Prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Binzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 周彝聞之，收軍而遁。

translations.literal: When Zhouyi heard of it he gathered his army and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Zhouyi gathered his men and fled.

sentences.zh: 茂貞既失鄜州之援，愕然有瓦解之懼，由是議還警蹕，誅閹寺以自贖焉。

translations.literal: Maozhen, having lost Binzhou's support, was stunned with fear of collapse and therefore discussed restoring the imperial carriage's vigilance and executing the eunuch officials to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of Bin's aid, Maozhen panicked at collapse and talked of restoring the imperial guard and killing the eunuchs to atone.

sentences.zh: 三年正月甲寅，岐人啟壁，唐昭宗降使宣問慰勞，兼傳密旨。

translations.literal: On jiayin in the first month of the third year the Qi opened their walls; Tang Emperor Zhaozong sent envoys to proclaim inquiries and comfort, and also conveyed secret instructions.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the third year's first month the Qi opened their gates; Zhaozong sent envoys with greetings and secret orders.

sentences.zh: 尋又命翰林學士韓渥、趙國夫人寵顏齎詔押賜帝紫金酒器、禦衣玉帶。

translations.literal: Soon he also ordered Han Wo, Hanlin academician, and the Zhao State Lady Chongyan to deliver imperial edicts and gifts to the Emperor of purple-gold wine vessels and an imperial jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Han Wo the Hanlin scholar and Lady Chongyan of Zhao were sent with edicts and gifts—purple-gold wine vessels and an imperial jade belt.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，華州留後李存審遣飛騎來告，青州節度使王師範遣牙將張厚輦甲胄弓槊，詐言來獻，欲盜據州城，事覺，已擒之矣。

translations.literal: On bingchen Hua Prefecture acting governor Li Cunshen sent swift riders to report: Qingzhou military governor Wang Shifan had sent tooth officer Zhang Hou arraying armor, bows, and lances, claiming to come in tribute but intending to seize the prefectural city by stealth—the plot was exposed and he had been captured.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Li Cunshen of Hua sent riders word that Wang Shifan of Qingzhou had sent Zhang Hou with arms under pretense of tribute to seize the city—the plot failed and Zhang was taken.

sentences.zh: 是日，師範又遣其將劉鄩盜據兗州。

translations.literal: That same day Shifan also sent his general Liu Yan to seize Yan Prefecture by stealth.
translations.idiomatic: That day Shifan also sent Liu Yan to take Yanzhou by stealth.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，昭宗遣中使押送軍容使韓全誨已下三千餘人首級以示帝。

translations.literal: On dingsi Zhaozong sent palace envoys escorting the heads of more than three thousand men including Army Commissioner Han Quanhui to present to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Zhaozong sent envoys bearing the heads of Han Quanhui and more than three thousand others.

sentences.zh: 甲子，昭宗發離鳳翔，幸左劍寨，權駐蹕帝營。

translations.literal: On jiazi Zhaozong departed Fengxiang for the Left Sword Stockade and provisionally halted at the Emperor's camp.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Zhaozong left Fengxiang for the Left Sword Stockade and paused at the Emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 帝素服待罪，昭宗命學士傳宣免之，帝即入見稱罪，拜伏者數四。

translations.literal: The Emperor wore plain robes awaiting punishment; Zhaozong had academicians proclaim his pardon, and the Emperor at once entered to confess guilt, bowing repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor waited in plain dress to plead guilt; Zhaozong pardoned him by edict, and he entered at once, bowing again and again.

sentences.zh: 既而促召升殿，密邇御座，且曰：「宗廟社稷是卿再造，朕與戚屬是卿再生。

translations.literal: Then he urgently summoned him up to the hall, close by the imperial seat, saying, "The ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain you have restored; I and my kin are reborn through you."
translations.idiomatic: He was quickly called up beside the throne: "You remade the temples and altars; you gave me and my kin new life."

sentences.zh: 」因解所御玉帶面以賜帝；

translations.literal: He removed the jade belt he wore and bestowed it on the Emperor face to face;
translations.idiomatic: He took the jade belt from his own waist and gave it to the Emperor in person;

sentences.zh: 帝亦以玉鞍勒馬、金銀器、紋錦、御饌酒果等躬自拜進焉。

translations.literal: the Emperor also personally presented a jade saddle, bridle, horse, gold and silver vessels, patterned brocade, imperial viands, wine, and fruit, bowing as he offered them.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor in turn bowed and presented a jade saddle and bridle, horse, gold and silver, brocade, and imperial food and wine.

sentences.zh: 及翠華東行，帝匹馬前導十餘里，宣令止之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went east, the Emperor rode alone ahead for more than ten li; an order was proclaimed to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: As the carriage moved east the Emperor rode ahead alone for ten li until a command bade him stop.

sentences.zh: 己巳，昭宗至長安，謁太廟，禦長樂樓。

translations.literal: On jisi Zhaozong reached Chang'an, visited the ancestral temple, and took his seat at Changle Tower.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Zhaozong entered Chang'an, worshipped at the ancestral temple, and ascended Changle Tower.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，謂帝曰：「朕生入舊京，是卿之力也。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished he said to the Emperor, "That I was born back into the old capital is your doing.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended he told the Emperor, "That I live again in the old capital is your work.

sentences.zh: 自古救君之危，曾無有如是者。

translations.literal: Since antiquity no rescue of a ruler in peril has ever been like this.
translations.idiomatic: Never in history was a sovereign rescued from peril as you have done."

sentences.zh: 況今日再及清廟，得親奉觴酒，奠于先皇帝室前，卿之德，朕知不能報矣！

translations.literal: Moreover, today to reach the Pure Temple again and personally offer libations before the former emperor's chamber—I know your merit cannot be repaid!"
translations.idiomatic: And today to reach the temple again and pour wine before my father's spirit—I know I can never repay you!"

sentences.zh: 」即召帝執手，聲淚俱發者久之。

translations.literal: He then took the Emperor's hand; voice and tears lasted long.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Emperor's hand and wept aloud for a long while.

sentences.zh: 翼日，誅宦官第五可范等五百餘人於內侍省。

translations.literal: The next day more than five hundred men including the eunuch Di Wu Kefan were executed in the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Next day more than five hundred including the eunuch Di Wu Kefan were executed in the Inner Service Directorate.

sentences.zh: 三月庚辰，制以帝為守太尉、兼中書令、宣武宣義天平護國等軍節度使、諸道兵馬副元師，加食邑三千戶，實封四百戶，仍賜回天再造竭忠守正功臣。

translations.literal: On gengchen in the third month an edict appointed the Emperor Defender Grand Marshal, concurrently Director of the Secretariat, military governor of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, Huguo, and other circuits, Vice Commander-in-chief of all circuits' armies, increased fief by three thousand households with four hundred actual, and bestowed the title of Meritious Minister Who Exhausted His Strength to Turn Back Heaven and Renew the Dynasty, Devotedly Upright.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen in the third month he was made Defender Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, governor of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, Huguo and other circuits, vice commander of all armies, with three thousand added households and four hundred actual, and the title Meritious Minister Who Turned Back Heaven and Renewed the Dynasty.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，帝建旆東還，昭宗御延喜樓送之，既醉，遣內臣賜帝御製《楊柳詞》五首。

translations.literal: On wuxu the Emperor raised his banners and returned east; Zhaozong went to Yanchi Tower to see him off, and when drunk dispatched inner retainers to gift the Emperor five personally composed "Willow Branch" lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the Emperor marched east; Zhaozong saw him off from Yanchi Tower and, drunk, sent five "Willow Branch" lyrics of his own composition.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午，至大樑。

translations.literal: On wuwu in the third month he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the third month he reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 時以青州未平，命軍士休浣以俟東征。

translations.literal: Because Qingzhou was not yet pacified, he ordered the troops to rest and wash gear awaiting the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: With Qingzhou still unrestored, he gave the army leave to rest and refit for the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 四月丙子，巡師於臨朐，亟命逼其城，與青州兵戰於城下，大敗之。

translations.literal: On bingzi in the fourth month he reviewed the army at Linqu and urgently ordered them to press the city; they fought Qingzhou troops below the walls and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi in the fourth month he reviewed troops at Linqu, pressed the city, and routed Qingzhou forces below the walls.

sentences.zh: 是夕，淮將王景仁以所部援軍宵遁，帝遣楊師厚追及輔唐，殺千人，乘勝攻下密州。

translations.literal: That evening Huainan general Wang Jingren fled by night with his relief division; the Emperor sent Yang Shihou to overtake him at Futang, killed a thousand men, and pressing the victory took Mi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That night Huainan's Wang Jingren fled with his relief; Yang Shihou overtook him at Futang, killed a thousand, and took Mizhou in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 八月戊辰，以伐叛之柄委于楊師厚，帝乃東還。

translations.literal: On wuchen in the eighth month he delegated authority to suppress rebellion to Yang Shihou, and the Emperor returned east.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the eighth month he gave Yang Shihou command of the pacification and returned east himself.

sentences.zh: 九月癸卯，師厚率大軍與王師範戰於臨朐，青軍大敗，殺萬餘人，並擒師範弟師克，即時徙寨以逼其城。

translations.literal: On guimao in the ninth month Shihou led a great army and fought Wang Shifan at Linqu; the Qing army was greatly defeated, more than ten thousand killed, and Shifan's younger brother Shike was captured; they immediately moved camps to press the city.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the ninth month Shihou met Wang Shifan at Linqu, crushed the Qing army, killed ten thousand, captured his brother Shike, and shifted camp to press the city.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，偏將劉重霸擒棣州刺史邵播來獻。

translations.literal: On xinhai the deputy general Liu Chongba captured Yan Prefecture governor Shao Bo and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Liu Chongba took Di governor Shao Bo and presented him.

sentences.zh: 播，師範之謀主也，帝命斃之。

translations.literal: Bo was Shifan's chief strategist; the Emperor ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was Shifan's chief plotter; the Emperor had him killed.

sentences.zh: 戊午，師範舉城請降。

translations.literal: On wuwu Shifan surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Shifan surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 青州平。

translations.literal: Qingzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 翼日，分命將校略地於登、萊、淄、棣等州，皆下之。

translations.literal: The next day he separately ordered officers to overrun the prefectures of Deng, Lai, Zi, and Di—all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Next day columns overran Deng, Lai, Zi, and Di—all submitted.

sentences.zh: 由是東漸至海，皆為梁土也。

translations.literal: Thus the east gradually to the sea all became Liang territory.
translations.idiomatic: The east to the sea was Liang soil thereafter.

sentences.zh: 帝復命師範權知青州軍州事，師範乃請以錢二十萬貫犒軍，帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor again appointed Shifan provisional governor of Qingzhou; Shifan requested twenty ten-thousands of strings of cash to reward the army, which the Emperor granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor left Shifan provisional governor of Qingzhou; Shifan offered two hundred thousand strings to reward the troops, and it was accepted.

sentences.zh: 十月辛巳，護駕都指揮使硃友倫因擊鞠墮馬，卒于長安。

translations.literal: On xinsi the Escort Commander Zhu Youlun died at Chang'an from falling off his horse while playing cuju.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Escort Commander Zhu Youlun died at Chang'an after falling from his horse at cuju.

sentences.zh: 訃至，帝大怒，以為唐室大臣欲謀叛己，致友倫暴死。

translations.literal: When the death notice arrived the Emperor was enraged, believing Tang court ministers wanted to rebel against him and had caused Youlun's violent death.
translations.idiomatic: When word came the Emperor raged, convinced Tang ministers had plotted against him and murdered Youlun.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁酉，青將劉鄩舉兗州來降。

translations.literal: On dingyou in the eleventh month Qing general Liu Yan surrendered Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in the eleventh month Liu Yan of Qing surrendered Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄩，王師範之將也，師範令竊據兗州久之，及聞師範降，鄩乃歸命。

translations.literal: Yan was Shifan's general; Shifan had long ordered him to hold Yan Prefecture by stealth, and when he heard Shifan had surrendered, Yan submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had long held Yanzhou for Shifan by stealth; hearing of Shifan's surrender, he submitted.

sentences.zh: 帝以鄩善事其主，待之甚優，尋署為元帥府都押牙，權知鄜州留後。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Yan served his lord well, treated him very generously and soon appointed him Grand Adjutant of the Marshal's Headquarters, acting Bin Prefecture regent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor prized Yan's loyalty, treated him generously, and soon made him chief adjutant of the marshal's staff and acting Bin regent.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年正月己酉，帝發自大梁，西赴河中，京師聞之，為之震懼。

translations.literal: On jiyou in the first month of the Tianyou first year the Emperor set out from Daliang west to Hezhong; the capital trembled at the news.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in Tianyou's first month he left Daliang for Hezhong; the capital shook at the news.

sentences.zh: 是時，將議迎駕東幸洛陽，慮唐室大臣異議，帝乃密令護駕都指揮使硃友諒矯昭宗命，收宰相崔允、京兆尹鄭元規等殺之。

translations.literal: At this time they planned to welcome the imperial carriage east to Luoyang and feared Tang ministers would object; the Emperor secretly ordered Escort Commander Zhu Youliang to forge Zhaozong's order and seize and kill Chancellor Cui Yun, Jingzhao Intendant Zheng Yuangui, and others.
translations.idiomatic: They planned to move the court east to Luoyang and feared Tang ministers would resist; secretly the Emperor had Zhu Youliang forge an order and kill Cui Yun, Zheng Yuangui, and others.

sentences.zh: 《歐陽史》云：遣硃謙殺胤于京師，其與友倫擊鞠者皆殺之。

translations.literal: The 《Ouyang Shi》 says: He sent Zhu Qian to kill Yin at the capital, and all who played cuju with Youlun were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Ouyang Shi》 says Zhu Qian killed Yin in the capital and all who had played cuju with Youlun were slain.

sentences.zh: 又，邠、岐兵士侵逼京畿，帝因是上表，堅請昭宗幸洛，昭宗不得已而從之。

translations.literal: Also, Bin and Qi soldiers pressed the capital region; the Emperor therefore memorialized urgently asking Zhaozong to go to Luo, and Zhaozong had no choice but to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and Qi troops also pressed the capital; the Emperor memorialized urgently for Zhaozong to go to Luo, and Zhaozong assented against his will.

sentences.zh: 帝乃率諸道丁匠財力，同構洛陽官，不數月而成。

translations.literal: The Emperor then led craftsmen and wealth from all circuits together to build Luoyang's palaces, completed within months.
translations.idiomatic: He then pooled craftsmen and wealth from every circuit to build Luoyang's palaces, finished within months.

sentences.zh: 二月乙亥，昭宗駐蹕於陝，帝自河中來覲，謁見行營。

translations.literal: On yihai in the second month Zhaozong halted at Shan; the Emperor came from Hezhong to pay homage and met him at the marching camp.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai in the second month Zhaozong paused at Shan; the Emperor came from Hezhong to meet him at camp.

sentences.zh: 因灑涕而言曰：「李茂貞等竊謀禍亂，將迫乘輿，老臣無狀，請陛下東遷，為社稷大計也。

translations.literal: Weeping he said, "Li Maozhen and others secretly plotted calamity and disorder, about to press the imperial carriage; your old servant was in the wrong in begging Your Majesty to migrate east—for the great plan of the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: In tears he said, "Li Maozhen plotted treason and would have seized you; this old servant begged you eastward only for the realm's sake."

sentences.zh: 」昭宗命延于寢室見何皇后，面賜酒器及衣物。

translations.literal: Zhaozong ordered him invited to the sleeping chamber to see Empress He and personally bestowed wine vessels and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong had him brought to the inner chamber to see Empress He and gave him wine vessels and robes.

sentences.zh: 何後謂帝曰：「此後大家夫婦委身于全忠矣。

translations.literal: The Empress said to the Emperor, "From now on the Imperial Couple entrust themselves to Quanzhong."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress told him, "Henceforth we two entrust ourselves to Quanzhong."

sentences.zh: 」因欷歔泣下。

translations.literal: She sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: She sighed and wept.

sentences.zh: 後數日，帝開宴於陝之私第，請駕臨幸。

translations.literal: Several days later the Emperor opened a banquet at his private residence in Shan and invited the imperial carriage to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he feasted at his private lodge in Shan and invited the emperor to attend.

sentences.zh: 翼日，帝辭歸洛陽，昭宗開內宴，時有宮人與昭宗附耳而語。

translations.literal: The next day when the Emperor took leave for Luoyang, Zhaozong opened an inner banquet; palace women whispered in Zhaozong's ear.
translations.idiomatic: Next day, as the Emperor left for Luoyang, Zhaozong held an inner feast; palace women whispered in his ear.

sentences.zh: 韓建躡帝之足，帝遽出，以為圖己，因連上章請車駕幸洛。

translations.literal: Han Jian trod on the Emperor's foot; the Emperor hastily withdrew, believing they plotted against him, and submitted memorial after memorial asking the carriage to go to Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian trod on his foot; the Emperor withdrew at once, suspecting a plot, and memorialized again and again for the move to Luo.

sentences.zh: 《十國春秋》、《吳世家》，三月丁巳，唐帝遣間使以絹詔告難於我及西川、河東等，令糾率籓鎮，以圖匡復。

translations.literal: The 《Shiguo Chunqiu》 and 《Wu Shijia》: On dingsi in the third month the Tang Emperor sent secret envoys with silk edicts announcing distress to us and to Western Shu, Hedong, and others, ordering them to rally the frontier commands for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Shiguo Chunqiu》 and 《Wu Shijia》 record that on dingsi in the third month secret envoys bore silk edicts of distress to us, Western Shu, Hedong, and others to rally the circuits for restoration.

sentences.zh: 詔有云：「朕至洛陽，則為全忠所幽閉，詔敕皆出其手，朕意不得復通矣。」

translations.literal: The edict said, "When I reach Luoyang I shall be confined by Quanzhong; edicts and orders all come from his hand—I fear my intent can no longer get through."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "At Luoyang Quanzhong will cage me; every order will be his—I shall no longer reach the realm."

sentences.zh: 三月丁未，昭宗制以帝兼判左右神策及六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: On dingwei in the third month Zhaozong's edict appointed the Emperor concurrently to judge the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and all Six Armies guards.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the third month Zhaozong named him to command the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and the Six Army guards.

sentences.zh: 是時，昭宗累遣中使及內夫人傳宣，謂帝曰：「皇后方在草蓐，未任就路，欲以十月幸洛。

translations.literal: At this time Zhaozong repeatedly sent palace envoys and inner ladies to proclaim to the Emperor, "The Empress is still in childbirth and cannot travel—she wishes to go to Luo in the tenth month."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong kept sending envoys and inner ladies to say the Empress was still confined and could not travel until the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 」帝以陝州小籓，非萬乘久留之地，期以四月內東幸。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Shan was a small fief and no place for the Son of Heaven to linger long, set the deadline for the eastern journey within the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was too small for the Son of Heaven to linger; he insisted on the move before the fourth month ended.

sentences.zh: 閏月丁酉，昭宗發自陝郡。

translations.literal: On dingyou in the intercalary month Zhaozong departed Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in the intercalary month Zhaozong left Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，次於谷水。

translations.literal: On renyin he halted at Gushui.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he camped at Gushui.

sentences.zh: 是時，昭宗左右惟小黃門及打球供奉、內園小兒二百餘人，帝猶忌之。

translations.literal: At this time Zhaozong's attendants were only minor yellow-gate eunuchs, cuju players in attendance, and inner-garden boys—more than two hundred in all—and the Emperor still feared them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhaozong's attendants were only junior eunuchs, cuju players, and inner-garden boys—over two hundred—and the Emperor still mistrusted them.

sentences.zh: 是日，密令醫官許昭遠告變，乃設饌於別幄，召而盡殺之，皆坑於幕下。

translations.literal: That day he secretly ordered the medical officer Xu Zhaoyuan to report a mutiny, set a feast in a separate tent, summoned them and killed them all, burying them in pits below the tent.
translations.idiomatic: That day he had the physician Xu Zhaoyuan cry mutiny, feasted them in a side tent, killed them all, and buried them in pits beneath it.

sentences.zh: 先是，選二百餘人，形貌大小一如內園人物之狀，至是使一人擒二人，縊於坑所，即蒙其衣及戎具自飾。

translations.literal: Earlier two hundred-odd men had been selected whose appearance and stature matched the inner-garden personnel; now one man seized two others and strangled them at the pit, then donned their clothes and military gear to disguise himself.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred men of matching build had been chosen; each seized two others, strangled them at the pit, and donned their dress and gear.

sentences.zh: 昭宗初不能辨，久而方察。

translations.literal: Zhaozong at first could not tell; only after long did he perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong noticed nothing at first; only after long did he see through it.

sentences.zh: 自是，昭宗左右前後，皆梁人矣。

translations.literal: From then on, before and behind and on every side of Zhaozong—all were Liang men.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth every attendant before and behind Zhaozong was a Liang man.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，車駕至洛都，帝與宰相百官導駕入宮。

translations.literal: On jiachen the imperial carriage reached Luoyang; the Emperor with chancellor and hundred officials guided the carriage into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the carriage entered Luoyang; the Emperor and the full court escorted it within.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，昭宗以帝為宣武、宣義、護國、忠武四鎮節度使。

translations.literal: On yimao Zhaozong appointed the Emperor military governor of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Huguo, and Zhongwu four circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Zhaozong made him governor of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Huguo, and Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 時帝請以鄆州授張全義，故有此命。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor had requested that Yan Prefecture be granted to Zhang Quanyi, hence this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had asked that Yanzhou be given to Zhang Quanyi—hence this order.

sentences.zh: 五月丙寅，昭宗宴群臣，曰：「昨來禦樓前一夜亡失赦書，賴梁王收得副本，不然誤事，宰執不得無過矣。

translations.literal: On bingyin in the fifth month Zhaozong feasted the ministers and said, "Last night before the imperial tower the amnesty edict was lost for a night; thanks to the Prince of Liang recovering a copy, otherwise affairs would have gone wrong—the chief ministers cannot be without fault."
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the fifth month Zhaozong feasted his ministers and said, "The amnesty edict vanished from the tower last night; only the Liang prince's copy saved us—the chief ministers are not blameless."

sentences.zh: 」是日宴次，昭宗入內，召帝于內殿曲宴，帝不測其事，不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: That day during the feast Zhaozong went within, summoned the Emperor to a private banquet in the inner hall; the Emperor could not fathom the matter and dared not obey the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-feast Zhaozong withdrew and summoned the Emperor to a private inner banquet; uneasy, he dared not go.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「卿不欲來，即令敬翔人來。

translations.literal: He also said, "If you do not wish to come, then have Jingxiang come in your stead."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If you will not come, send Jingxiang."

sentences.zh: 」帝密遣翔出，乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly sent Xiang out, and only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor quietly sent Xiang in his place, and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 己巳，奉辭東歸。

translations.literal: On jisi he took leave and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he took his leave and marched east.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，至大樑。

translations.literal: On yihai he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai he arrived at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝遣都將硃友裕率師討邠州，節度使楊崇本叛故也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor sent Chief Commander Zhu Youyu to lead troops to attack Bin Prefecture, because Military Governor Yang Chongben had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he sent Zhu Youyu against Binzhou—Yang Chongben, its governor, had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，帝西征，遂朝於洛陽。

translations.literal: On guichou the Emperor campaigned west and then paid court at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he marched west and attended court at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 七月甲子，昭宗宴帝于文思鞠場。

translations.literal: On jiazi in the seventh month Zhaozong feasted the Emperor at the Wensi cuju ground.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi in the seventh month Zhaozong entertained him at the Wensi ball ground.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，帝發東都。

translations.literal: On yichou the Emperor departed the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he left Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 壬申，至河中。

translations.literal: On renshen he reached Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he reached Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 八月壬寅，昭宗遇弑於大內，遺制以輝王柷為嗣。

translations.literal: On renyin in the eighth month Zhaozong was assassinated in the inner palace; his testamentary decree named Prince Hui Zhu as successor.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin in the eighth month assassins killed Zhaozong in the palace; his dying decree made Prince Hui Zhu heir.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，帝自河中引軍而西。

translations.literal: On yisi the Emperor led his army west from Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi he marched west from Hezhong with his army.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，次於永壽，邠軍不出。

translations.literal: On guichou he halted at Yongshou; the Bin army did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he camped at Yongshou, but the Bin forces refused battle.

sentences.zh: 九月辛未，班師。

translations.literal: On xinwei in the ninth month he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the ninth month he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十月癸巳，至洛陽，詣西內，臨于梓宮前，祗見於嗣君。

translations.literal: On guisi in the tenth month he reached Luoyang, went to the western inner palace, stood before the bier, and paid homage to the new sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi in the tenth month he entered Luoyang, mourned before the bier in the western palace, and bowed to the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，制以案此下有闕文。

translations.literal: On xinchou an edict was issued—note: text is missing below this point.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou an edict was promulgated; the text below is lost in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 帝至自西征。

translations.literal: The Emperor returned from the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor returned from the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛酉，光州遣使來求援。

translations.literal: On xinyou in the eleventh month Guang Prefecture sent envoys to beg for aid.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou in the eleventh month Guangzhou sent envoys pleading for help.

sentences.zh: 時光州歸款於帝，尋為淮人所攻，故來乞師。

translations.literal: At this time Guang Prefecture had submitted to the Emperor but was soon attacked by the Huai people, and so came to beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou had just submitted when Huainan forces attacked—hence the plea for troops.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，帝南征渡淮，次於霍丘，大掠盧、壽之境，淮人乃棄光州而去。

translations.literal: On wuyin the Emperor campaigned south, crossed the Huai, halted at Huoqiu, and ravaged the lands of Lu and Shou; the Huai people then abandoned Guang Prefecture and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he crossed the Huai, camped at Huoqiu, and plundered Lu and Shou until the Huai army abandoned Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年正月庚申，進攻壽州，壽人堅壁不出。

translations.literal: On gengshen in the first month of the second year he attacked Shou Prefecture; the people of Shou held their walls and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the second year's first month he besieged Shouzhou; the defenders refused to sally.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，帝自霍丘班師。

translations.literal: On dinghai the Emperor withdrew his army from Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he withdrew from Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 二月辛卯，帝至自南征。

translations.literal: On xinmao in the second month the Emperor returned from the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the second month he returned from the south.

sentences.zh: 甲午，青州節度使王師範至大樑，帝待以賓禮，尋表授河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On jiawu Military Governor Wang Shifan of Qingzhou came to Daliang; the Emperor received him with guest rites and soon memorialized appointing him military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Wang Shifan of Qingzhou arrived at Daliang; the Emperor treated him as an honored guest and soon named him governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 七月辛酉，天子賜帝迎鸞紀功碑，樹於洛陽。

translations.literal: On xinyou in the seventh month the Son of Heaven bestowed on the Emperor a stele commemorating the welcoming of the imperial carriage, erected at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the court gave him a stele commemorating the imperial welcome, set up at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 庚午，遣大將軍楊師厚率前軍討趙匡凝於襄州。

translations.literal: On gengwu he sent Grand General Yang Shihou to lead the vanguard to attack Zhao Kuangning at Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he sent Yang Shihou with the vanguard against Zhao Kuangning at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝南征，表趙匡凝罪狀，削奪官爵。

translations.literal: On xinwei the Emperor campaigned south, memorialized listing Zhao Kuangning's crimes, and stripped him of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he marched south, denounced Zhao Kuangning in a memorial, and stripped his titles.

sentences.zh: 八月，楊師厚進收唐、鄧、復、郢、隨、均、房等七州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Yang Shihou advanced and recovered Tang, Deng, Fu, Ying, Sui, Jun, and Fang—seven prefectures in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Yang Shihou seized Tang, Deng, Fu, Ying, Sui, Jun, and Fang—seven prefectures.

sentences.zh: 帝駐軍漢江北，自循江幹，經度濟師之所。

translations.literal: The Emperor encamped north of the Han River, himself following the riverbank to inspect the crossing places.
translations.idiomatic: He camped north of the Han and walked the bank himself, choosing where the army would cross.

sentences.zh: 九月甲子，師厚于陰谷江口造梁以濟師，趙匡凝率兵二萬振于江濱。

translations.literal: On jiazi in the ninth month Shihou built a bridge at Yingu River mouth to ferry the army; Zhao Kuangning led twenty thousand men and arrayed them along the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Shihou bridged the Yingu mouth; Zhao Kuangning drew up twenty thousand men on the far bank.

sentences.zh: 師厚麾兵進擊，襄人大敗，殺萬餘眾。

translations.literal: Shihou waved his troops forward in attack; the Xiang people were greatly defeated, more than ten thousand slain.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou charged; the Xiang army broke with ten thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，越匡凝焚其舟，率親軍載輕舸沿漢而遁。

translations.literal: On yichou Zhao Kuangning burned his boats, led his personal guard aboard light craft, and fled up the Han.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Zhao Kuangning burned his fleet and fled up the Han in light boats with his guard.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，帝濟江，至中流，舟壞，將沒者數四，比及岸，舟沉。

translations.literal: On bingyin the Emperor crossed the river; midstream the boat broke, and he nearly drowned four times; by the time he reached shore the boat had sunk.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin he crossed mid-river when the boat gave way—four times he nearly went under—and reached shore only as it sank.

sentences.zh: 是日，入襄城，帝因周視府署，其帑藏悉空。

translations.literal: That day he entered Xiang city; the Emperor thereupon toured the prefectural offices—their treasuries were entirely empty.
translations.idiomatic: That day he entered Xiangcheng and toured the yamen; every storehouse stood empty.

sentences.zh: 惟於西廡下有一亭，窗戶儼然，扃鎖甚密，遂令破鎖啟扉，中有一大匱，緘鐍甚至；

translations.literal: Only under the western corridor was a pavilion whose windows stood intact, locked very tight; he ordered the lock broken and the door opened—within was a great chest, sealed with extraordinary care;
translations.idiomatic: Only a pavilion under the west corridor remained intact, heavily locked; when they broke the seal they found a great chest, bound shut;

sentences.zh: 又令破其匱，內有金銀數百錠。

translations.literal: he ordered the chest broken open as well; inside were several hundred ingots of gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: and inside several hundred ingots of gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 帝因歎曰：「亂兵既入，公私財貨固無孑遺矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon sighed and said, "Once the mutinous soldiers entered, public and private wealth surely left not a scrap.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "When the mutineers came through, public and private wealth vanished to the last scrap.

sentences.zh: 此帑當有陰物主之，不令常人所得，俟我以有之邪！

translations.literal: This treasury must have had a hidden power guarding it, not letting ordinary men obtain it—was it waiting for me to possess it!"
translations.idiomatic: Some hidden hand kept this hoard from common looters—was it waiting for me?"

sentences.zh: 」遂以百餘錠賜楊師厚。

translations.literal: He then bestowed more than a hundred ingots on Yang Shihou.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Yang Shihou more than a hundred ingots.

sentences.zh: 襲荊州，留後趙匡明棄城上峽奔蜀。

translations.literal: They struck Jing Prefecture; Acting Governor Zhao Kuangming abandoned the city, went up the gorges, and fled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou fell; Zhao Kuangming abandoned the city, fled upriver into the gorges, and escaped to Shu.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄二州平。

translations.literal: Jing and Xiang two prefectures were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Xiang were pacified.

sentences.zh: 帝以都將賀瑰權領荊州，楊師厚權領襄州，即表其事。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Chief Commander He Gui provisionally lead Jing Prefecture and Yang Shihou provisionally lead Xiang Prefecture, and immediately memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He left He Gui in charge at Jingzhou and Yang Shihou at Xiangzhou and memorialized the appointments at once.

sentences.zh: 十月丙戌朔，天子以帝為諸道兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: On the bingxu new moon in the tenth month the Son of Heaven appointed the Emperor commander-in-chief of all circuits' military forces.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth month's new moon the court named him commander-in-chief of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，帝自襄州引軍由光州路趨淮南；

translations.literal: On xinmao the Emperor led his army from Xiang Prefecture by the Guang Prefecture route toward Huainan;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he marched from Xiangzhou toward Huainan by way of Guangzhou;

sentences.zh: 將發，敬翔切諫，請班師以全軍勢，帝不聽。
